title: Neural algorithmic reasoning
title_zh: 经典计算与深度神经网络

paragraphs.en: In this article, we will talk about classical computation : the kind of computation typically found in an undergraduate Computer Science course on Algorithms and Data Structures [1]. Think shortest path-finding, sorting, clever ways to break problems down into simpler problems, incredible ways to organise data for efficient retrieval and updates. Of course, given The Gradient ’s focus on Artificial Intelligence, we will not stop there; we will also investigate how to capture such computation with deep neural networks.
paragraphs.zh: 在本文中，我们将讨论经典计算：即本科计算机科学专业的算法与数据结构课程中常见的计算类型 [1]。 想想最短路径查找、排序、把问题分解为更简单问题的巧妙方法，以及为高效检索和更新而组织数据的绝佳方式。 当然，鉴于 The Gradient 专注于人工智能，我们不会止步于此；我们还将研究如何用深度神经网络来捕捉这类计算。

paragraphs.en: Maybe it’s worth starting by clarifying where my vested interest in classical computation comes from. Competitive programming—the art of solving problems by rapidly writing programs that need to terminate in a given amount of time, and within certain memory constraints—was a highly popular activity in my secondary school. For me, it was truly the gateway into Computer Science, and I trust the story is similar for many machine learning practitioners and researchers today. I have been able to win several medals at international programming competitions, such as the Northwestern Europe Regionals of the ACM-ICPC, the top-tier Computer Science competition for university students. Hopefully, my successes in competitive programming also give me some credentials to write about this topic.
paragraphs.zh: 或许值得先澄清一下，我对经典计算的切身利益从何而来。 竞赛编程——即通过快速编写程序来解题的艺术，这些程序需要在给定时间内、在特定内存限制下终止运行——在我的中学时代是一项非常流行的活动。 对我来说，它真正是通往计算机科学的大门，我相信今天许多机器学习从业者和研究人员的经历也是如此。 我曾在国际编程竞赛中赢得多枚奖牌，例如 ACM-ICPC 西北欧区域赛，这是面向大学生的顶级计算机科学竞赛。 希望我在竞赛编程上的成绩也能让我在撰写这个话题时具备一些资历。

paragraphs.en: Looking at all of these properties taken together, they seem to be exactly the issues that plague modern deep neural networks the most: you can rarely guarantee their accuracy, they often collapse on out-of-distribution inputs, and they are very notorious as black boxes, with compounding errors that can hinder compositionality.
paragraphs.zh: 将所有这些性质放在一起看，它们似乎正是最困扰现代深度神经网络的问题：你很难保证它们的准确性，它们在分布外输入上常常失效，而且它们作为黑箱是出了名的，其累积误差会阻碍组合性。

paragraphs.en: However, it is exactly those skills that are important for making AI instructive and useful to humans! For example, to have an AI system that reliably and instructively teaches a concept to a human, the quality of its output should not depend on minor details of the input, and it should be able to generalise that concept to novel situations. Arguably, these skills are also a missing key step on the road to building generally-intelligent agents. Therefore, if we are able to make any strides towards capturing traits of classical computation in deep neural networks, this is likely to be a very fruitful pursuit.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，恰恰是这些技能对于让AI对人类具有指导性并发挥作用至关重要！ 例如，要让一个AI系统能够可靠且有指导性地向人类教授某个概念，其输出的质量不应依赖于输入的细微细节，并且它应能将该概念泛化到新颖的情境中。 可以说，这些技能也是构建通用智能体道路上缺失的关键一步。 因此，如果我们能够在深度神经网络中捕捉经典计算的特质方面取得任何进展，这很可能是一项非常富有成效的追求。

paragraphs.en: Here, we can see a visual decomposition of how a graph neural network ( GNN ) [3] aligns with the classical Bellman-Ford [4] algorithm for shortest path-finding. Specifically, Bellman-Ford maintains its current estimate of how far away each node is from the source node: a distance variable ( du ) for each node u in a graph. At every step, for every neighbour v of node u , an update to du is proposed: a combination of (optimally) reaching v , and then traversing the edge connecting v and u ( du + wvu ). The distance variable is then updated as the optimal out of all the proposals. Operations of a graph neural network can naturally decompose to follow the data flow of Bellman-Ford:
paragraphs.zh: 在这里，我们可以看到一个直观的分解图，展示了图神经网络（GNN）[3]如何与求解最短路径的经典 Bellman-Ford [4] 算法相对应。 具体来说，Bellman-Ford 会维护每个节点到源节点距离的当前估计值：即图中每个节点 u 对应的一个距离变量（du）。 在每一步，对于节点 u 的每个邻居 v，都会提出一个对 du 的更新：即（以最优方式）到达 v，再遍历连接 v 和 u 的边（du + wvu）。 随后，距离变量会被更新为所有提议中的最优值。 图神经网络的运算可以自然地分解为遵循 Bellman-Ford 的数据流：

paragraphs.en: Generally, it can be proven that, the more closely we can decompose our neural network to follow the algorithm’s structure , the more favourable sample complexity we can expect when learning to execute such algorithms. Bellman-Ford is a typical instance of a dynamic programming ( DP ) algorithm [5], a general-purpose problem-solving strategy that breaks the problem down into subproblems, and then recombines their solutions to find the final solution.
paragraphs.zh: 一般来说，可以证明，我们越能将神经网络分解得贴近算法的结构，在学习执行此类算法时就能期望越有利的样本复杂度。 Bellman-Ford 是动态规划（DP）算法 [5] 的一个典型实例，动态规划是一种通用的问题求解策略，它将问题分解为子问题，然后重新组合这些子问题的解以求得最终解。

paragraphs.en: In this paper [7], concurrently released with Xu et al. [2], we conducted a thorough empirical analysis of learning to execute with GNNs. We found that while algorithmic alignment is indeed a powerful tool for model class selection, it unfortunately does not allow us to be reckless . Namely, we cannot just apply any expressive GNN to an algorithmic execution task and expect great results, especially out-of-distribution —which we previously identified as a key setting in which “true” reasoning systems should perform well. Much like other neural networks, GNNs can very easily overfit to the characteristics of the distribution of training inputs, learning “clever hacks” and sidestepping the actual procedure that they are attempting to execute.
paragraphs.zh: 在本文 [7]（与 Xu et al. [2] 同期发表）中，我们对使用图神经网络（GNN）学习执行进行了全面的实证分析。我们发现，尽管算法对齐确实是选择模型类别的有力工具，但遗憾的是它并不能让我们肆意妄为。也就是说，我们不能随意将任何具有表达力的 GNN 应用于算法执行任务并期待出色的结果，尤其是在分布外场景——我们此前已将此确定为“真正的”推理系统应当表现良好的关键设定。与其他神经网络一样，GNN 非常容易过拟合于训练输入分布的特征，学会“取巧的捷径”，从而绕过它们试图执行的真正流程。

paragraphs.en: It must be stressed that the intuitive idea of algorithmic alignment—taking inspiration from Computer Science concepts in architecture design—is by no means novel! The text-book example of this are the neural Turing machine ( NTM ) and differentiable neural computer ( DNC ) [13, 14]. These works are decisively influential; in fact, in its attempt to make random-access memory compatible with gradient-based optimisation, the NTM gave us one of the earliest forms of content-based attention , three years before Transformers [15]!
paragraphs.zh: 必须强调的是，算法对齐的直观想法——在架构设计中从计算机科学概念中汲取灵感——绝非新颖！ 教科书式的例子就是神经图灵机（NTM）和可微分神经计算机（DNC）[13, 14]。 这些工作具有决定性的影响力；事实上，NTM 在试图使随机存取存储器与基于梯度的优化兼容的过程中，为我们提供了最早形式之一的基于内容的注意力，比 Transformer [15] 早了三年！

paragraphs.en: However, despite their influence, these architectures are nowadays virtually never used in practice. There are many possible causes for this, but in my opinion it is because their design was too brittle : trying to introduce many differentiable components into the same architecture at once, without a clear guidance on how to compose them, or a way to easily debug them once they failed to show useful signal on a new task. Our line of work still wants to build something like an NTM—but make it more successfully deployed, by using algorithmic alignment to more carefully prototype each building block in isolation, and have a more granular view of which blocks benefit execution of which target algorithms.

paragraphs.en: Our approach of “playing the algorithmic alignment game” appears to have yielded a successful line of specialised (G)NNs, and we now have worthy ‘fine-grained’ solutions for learning to execute linearithmic sequence algorithms [16], iterative algorithms [17], pointer-based data structures [18], as well as persistent auxiliary memory [19]. Eventually, these insights also carried over to more fine-grained theory as well. In light of our NEGA paper [7], the inventors of algorithmic alignment refined their theory into what is now known as linear algorithmic alignment [10], providing justification for, among other things, our use of the max aggregation. More recent insights show that understanding algorithmic alignment may require causal reasoning [20,21], properly formalising it may require category theory [22], and properly describing it may require analysing asynchronous computation [23]. Algorithmic alignment is therefore turning into a very exciting area for mathematical approaches to deep learning in recent years.
paragraphs.zh: 我们这种“玩转算法对齐博弈”的方法似乎已经催生了一系列成功的专用 (G)NN，如今我们拥有了值得称道的“细粒度”解决方案，可用于学习执行线性对数复杂度的序列算法 [16]、迭代算法 [17]、基于指针的数据结构 [18]，以及持久性辅助存储器 [19]。 最终，这些洞见也延伸到了更细粒度的理论之中。 鉴于我们的 NEGA 论文 [7]，算法对齐的提出者将其理论完善为如今所谓的线性算法对齐 [10]，除其他内容外，还为我们使用最大聚合（max aggregation）提供了理论依据。 更近期的洞见表明，理解算法对齐可能需要因果推理 [20,21]，恰当地将其形式化可能需要范畴论 [22]，而恰当地描述它可能需要分析异步计算 [23]。 因此，近年来算法对齐正在成为深度学习数学方法中一个非常令人兴奋的研究领域。

paragraphs.en: This is clearly not the nicest thing to receive as the first author of a paper. But still, let’s try to put my ego aside, and see what can be taken away from such reviews. There is a clear sense in which such reviews are raising an entirely valid point: tautologically , the target algorithm will execute itself better (or equally good) than any GNN we’d ever learn over it. Clearly, if we want wide-spread recognition of these ideas, we need to show how learning to execute can be usefully applied beyond the context of “pure” execution.
paragraphs.zh: 作为论文的第一作者，收到这样的评价显然不是什么令人愉快的事。 尽管如此，我们还是试着把我的自尊心放到一边，看看能从这样的审稿意见中得到什么。 这些审稿意见明确地提出了一个完全合理的观点：同义反复地说，目标算法执行自身的效果总会好于（或至少不差于）我们在其之上训练出的任何 GNN。 显然，如果我们想让这些想法得到广泛认可，就需要展示「学习执行」在“纯”执行场景之外还能如何得到有效的应用。

paragraphs.en: Our exploration led us to many possible ideas, and in the remainder of this article, I will show three ideas that saw the most impact.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的探索带来了许多可能的设想，在本文的剩余部分，我将展示其中影响力最大的三个设想。

paragraphs.en: First, algorithmically aligned models can accelerate science . And if you want clear evidence of this, look no further than the cover of Nature [24]. In our work, we train (G)NNs to fit a mathematical dataset of interest to a mathematician, and then use simple gradient saliency methods to signal to the mathematician which parts of the inputs to focus their attention at. While such signals are often remarkably noisy, they do allow a mathematician to study only the most salient 20-30 nodes in a graph that would otherwise have hundreds or thousands of nodes, making pattern discovery much easier. The discovered patterns can then form the basis of novel theorems, and/or be used to derive conjectures.
paragraphs.zh: 首先，经过算法对齐的模型可以加速科学的发展。 如果你想要这方面的明确证据，只需看看《自然》（Nature）杂志的封面 [24] 即可。 在我们的工作中，我们训练（图）神经网络来拟合数学家感兴趣的数学数据集，然后使用简单的梯度显著性方法向数学家发出信号，提示他们应将注意力集中在输入的哪些部分。 虽然这类信号通常噪声很大，但它们确实能让数学家只研究图中最显著的 20-30 个节点，否则图中可能有成百上千个节点，从而使模式发现变得容易得多。 发现的模式随后可以构成新定理的基础，和/或用于推导猜想。

paragraphs.en: With this simple approach, we were able to drive independent contributions to two highly disparate areas of math: knot theory [25] and representation theory [26], both subsequently published in their areas’ respective top-tier journals, hence earning us the Nature accolade. But, while our approach is simple in principle, a question arose especially in the representation theory branch: which (G)NN to use ? Standard expressive GNNs did not yield clearly interpretable results.
paragraphs.zh: 借助这一简单的方法，我们得以在数学中两个差异极大的领域做出独立贡献：纽结理论 [25] 和表示论 [26]，二者随后分别发表在各自领域的顶级期刊上，因此我们获得了《自然》的赞誉。 但是，尽管我们的方法在原理上很简单，特别是在表示论这一分支中出现了一个问题：应该使用哪种（图）神经网络？ 标准的高表达力图神经网络并未给出清晰可解释的结果。

paragraphs.en: This is where algorithmic alignment helped us: Geordie Williamson, our representation theory collaborator, provided an algorithm that would compute the outputs we care about, if we had access to privileged information. We achieved our best results with a GNN model that was explicitly aligning its components to this target algorithm.
paragraphs.zh: 这正是算法对齐帮助我们的地方：我们的表示论合作者乔治·威廉姆森提供了一个算法，如果我们能够获得特权信息，它就能计算出我们所关心的输出。 我们用 GNN 模型取得了最佳结果，该模型将其各个组件显式地对齐到这一目标算法上。

paragraphs.en: More generally: in this case, a target algorithm existed, but executing it was inapplicable (due to privileged inputs). Algorithmic alignment allowed us to embed “priors” from it anyway.

paragraphs.en: Second, algorithmically aligned models are fast heuristics . In recent work with computer networking and machine learning collaborators from ETH Zürich, we studied the applicability of neural algorithmic reasoning in computer networking [27]. Specifically, we sought to expedite the challenging task of configuration synthesis : based on a given specification of constraints a computer network should satisfy, produce a corresponding network configuration (a graph specifying the routers in a network and their connections). This configuration must satisfy all of the specifications, once a network protocol has been executed over it.
paragraphs.zh: 其次，经算法对齐的模型是快速的启发式方法。 在近期与苏黎世联邦理工学院（ETH Zürich）计算机网络和机器学习领域合作者的工作中，我们研究了神经算法推理在计算机网络中的应用 [27]。 具体而言，我们试图加速配置合成这一具有挑战性的任务：基于给定的一组计算机网络应满足的约束规范，生成相应的网络配置（一个指明网络中路由器及其连接关系的图）。 一旦在网络上执行了网络协议，该配置就必须满足所有规范。

sents.en: This configuration must satisfy all of the specifications, once a network protocol has been executed over it.
sents.zh: 一旦在网络上执行了网络协议，该配置就必须满足所有规范。

paragraphs.en: Producing these configurations is known to be a very challenging NP-hard problem—in practice, it is usually solved with slow SMT solvers, which can often require doubly-exponential complexity. Instead, we choose to use ideas from algorithmic reasoning to generate configurations by inverting the protocol (which can be seen as a graph algorithm). Specifically, we generate many random network configurations, execute the protocol over them, and collect all true facts about the resulting network to extract corresponding specifications. This gives us all we need to generate a graph-based dataset from specifications to configurations, and fit an algorithmically-aligned GNN to this dataset.
paragraphs.zh: 生成这些配置已知是一个非常困难的 NP-hard 问题——实践中通常使用缓慢的 SMT 求解器来解决，这类求解器往往需要双指数级的复杂度。 相反，我们选择利用算法推理的思想，通过反转协议（可视为一种图算法）来生成配置。 具体而言，我们生成大量随机网络配置，在其上执行协议，并收集所得网络的所有真实事实，以提取相应的规范。 这为我们提供了从规范生成配置的基于图的数据集所需的一切，并在该数据集上拟合一个与算法对齐的图神经网络（GNN）。

paragraphs.en: Naturally, by virtue of just requiring a forward pass of a machine learning model, this approach is substantially faster than SMT solvers at inference time: for certain configurations, we have observed over 490x speedup over the prior state-of-the-art. Of course, there is no free lunch: the price we pay for this speedup are occasional inaccuracies in the produced configurations at test-time. That being said, on all the relevant distributions we evaluated, the average number of constraints satisfied has consistently been over 90%, which makes our method already applicable for downstream human-in-the-loop use—and it is likely to accelerate human designers, as very often, the initial configurations are unsatisfiable , meaning SMT solvers will spend a lot of effort only to say a satisfying configuration cannot be found. During this time, a fast forward pass of a GNN could have allowed for far more rapid iteration.

paragraphs.en: Chances are, especially if you come from a theoretical Computer Science background like me, that you will respond to this question in a very singular way. paragraphs.en: This issue gets significantly tricker if the data is partially observable , there are adversarial actors in the environment, etc. I must stress that this is not an issue theoretical computer scientists tend to concern themselves with, and probably for good reason! paragraphs.en: This kind of pipeline is remarkably popular [34]; in recent times, there have been seminal results allowing for backpropagating through the encoder even when the algorithm itself is non-differentiable [35]. However, it suffers from an algorithmic bottleneck problem: namely, it is fully committing itself to the algorithm’s outputs [36]. That is, if the inputs to the algorithm are poorly predicted by the encoder, we run into the same issue as before—the algorithm will give a perfect answer in an incorrect environment. Since the required inputs are usually scalar in nature (e.g. a single distance per edge of the input graph), the encoder is often tasked with mapping the extremely rich structure of real world data into only a single number. This particularly becomes an issue with low-data or partially-observable scenarios.
paragraphs.zh: 这类流程极为流行 [34]；近期已有一些开创性成果，使得即使在算法本身不可微的情况下，也能通过编码器进行反向传播 [35]。 然而，它存在一个算法瓶颈问题：即它完全依赖于算法的输出 [36]。 也就是说，如果算法的输入被编码器预测得很差，我们就会遇到与之前相同的问题——算法会在错误的环境中给出完美的答案。 由于所需的输入通常是标量性质的（例如输入图的每条边仅对应一个距离），编码器往往需要将真实世界数据极为丰富的结构映射为仅仅一个数字。 这在低数据量或部分可观测的场景中尤其成为问题。

paragraphs.en: To break the algorithmic bottleneck, we instead opt to represent both the encoder and the algorithm as high-dimensional neural networks! Now, our algorithmic model is a processor neural network—mapping high dimensional embeddings to high dimensional embeddings. paragraphs.en: While initially only a proposal, there are now several successful NAR instances that have been published at top-tier venues [36,39,40,41]. In the most-recent such paper [41], we aimed to study how to classify blood vessels in the mouse brain—a very challenging graph task spanning millions of nodes and edges [42]. However, while it’s not trivial to directly classify blood vessels from their features, it is reasonably safe to assume that the main purpose of blood vessels is to conduct blood flow—hence, an algorithm for flow analysis could be a suitable one to deploy here. Accordingly, we first pre-trained a NAR processor to execute the relevant maximum-flow and minimum-cut algorithms [43], then successfully deployed it on the brain vessel graph, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art GNNs. It is worthy to note that the brain vessel graph is 180,000x larger than the synthetic graphs we used for learning to execute, and minimal hyperparameter tuning was applied throughout! We are confident this success is only the first of many.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然最初只是一个提案，但如今已有若干成功的 NAR 实例发表在顶级学术会议和期刊上 [36,39,40,41]。 在最近的一篇此类论文 [41] 中，我们旨在研究如何对小鼠大脑中的血管进行分类——这是一项极具挑战性的图任务，涉及数百万个节点和边 [42]。 然而，虽然直接根据血管的特征对血管进行分类并非易事，但可以比较稳妥地假设血管的主要功能是输送血流——因此，用于流分析的算法可能是在此部署的合适选择。 相应地，我们首先预训练了一个 NAR 处理器来执行相关的最大流和最小割算法 [43]，然后将其成功部署在大脑血管图上，超越了之前最先进的 GNN。 值得注意的是，大脑血管图比我们用于学习执行的合成图大 180,000 倍，而且整个过程几乎没有进行超参数调优！ 我们相信，这一成功只是众多成功中的第一个。

paragraphs.en: While the ideas given in prior subsections hopefully provide a good argument for the utility of capturing classical computation, in practice we still need to know which computation to capture ! All of the NAR papers referenced above use target algorithms highly relevant to the downstream task, and the processors are trained using bespoke execution datasets built on top of those algorithms. This often requires both domain expertise and computer science expertise, and hence represents a clear barrier of entry !
paragraphs.zh: 虽然前面各小节给出的观点 Hopefully（希望）能为捕获经典计算的实用性提供一个很好的论证，但在实践中我们仍然需要知道要捕获哪种计算！ 上面引用的所有 NAR 论文都使用与下游任务高度相关的目标算法，并且处理器是使用基于这些算法构建的定制执行数据集来训练的。 这通常既需要领域专业知识，也需要计算机科学专业知识，因此构成了一个明显的准入门槛！

paragraphs.en: Since my beginnings in NAR, I have been strongly interested in reducing this barrier of entry, while also providing a collection of “base processors” that should be useful in a wide variety of tasks. This resulted in a two-year-long engineering effort, culminating by open-sourcing the CLRS Algorithmic Reasoning Benchmark ( https://github.com/deepmind/clrs ) [44].
paragraphs.zh: 自我在 NAR 的起步阶段起，我就一直对降低这一入门门槛抱有浓厚兴趣，同时也希望提供一系列应在各种任务中都很有用的「基础处理器」。 这促成了一项历时两年的工程努力，最终以开源 CLRS 算法推理基准（ https://github.com/deepmind/clrs ）[44] 达到顶峰。

sents.en: This resulted in a two-year-long engineering effort, culminating by open-sourcing the CLRS Algorithmic Reasoning Benchmark ( https://github.com/deepmind/clrs ) [44].
sents.zh: 这促成了一项历时两年的工程努力，最终以开源 CLRS 算法推理基准（ https://github.com/deepmind/clrs ）[44] 达到顶峰。

paragraphs.en: The CLRS benchmark was inspired by the iconic Introduction to Algorithms (CLRS) textbook from C ormen, L eiserson, R ivest and S tein [1], which is one of the most popular undergraduate textbooks on classical algorithms and data structures, and a “bible” for competitive programmers. Despite its many thousands of pages, it only contains ~90 distinct algorithms, and these algorithms tend to form the foundations behind entire careers in software engineering! Hence, the algorithms in CLRS can form our desired solid set of “base processors”, and we set out to make it easy to construct and train NAR processors to execute the algorithms in CLRS.
paragraphs.zh: CLRS 基准测试的灵感来自 Cormen、Leiserson、Rivest 和 Stein 的经典著作《算法导论》（CLRS）教科书 [1]，该书是最受欢迎的经典算法与数据结构本科教科书之一，也是竞赛程序员的“圣经”。 尽管它有数千页的篇幅，但只包含约 90 种不同的算法，而这些算法往往构成了软件工程整个职业生涯的基础！ 因此，CLRS 中的算法可以构成我们期望的坚实的“基础处理器”集合，我们着手让构建和训练用于执行 CLRS 中算法的 NAR 处理器变得容易。

paragraphs.en: In its first incarnation, we released CLRS-30, a collection of dataset and processor generators for thirty algorithms in CLRS, spanning a wide variety of skills: sorting, searching, dynamic programming, graph algorithms, string algorithms and geometric algorithms.
paragraphs.zh: 在其第一个版本中，我们发布了 CLRS-30，这是一个针对 CLRS 中三十种算法的数据集与处理器生成器集合，涵盖多种技能领域：排序、搜索、动态规划、图算法、字符串算法和几何算法。

paragraphs.en: What makes CLRS-30 special is the wide variety of data, models and pipelines it exposes to the user: given an appropriate specification of the target algorithm’s variables, an implementation of the target algorithm, and a desirable random input sampler, CLRS will automatically produce the full execution trajectories of this algorithm’s variables in a spatio-temporal graph-structured format, relevant encoder/decoder/processor models, and loss functions. For this reason, we typically refer to CLRS as a “dataset and baseline generator ” rather than an individual dataset.
paragraphs.zh: CLRS-30 的特别之处在于它向用户提供了丰富多样的数据、模型和流水线：只要给出目标算法变量的适当规范、目标算法的一种实现，以及一个理想的随机输入采样器，CLRS 就会自动以时空图结构格式生成该算法变量的完整执行轨迹、相关的编码器/解码器/处理器模型，以及损失函数。 出于这个原因，我们通常将 CLRS 称为「数据集与基线生成器」，而不是一个单独的数据集。

By default, these can be used for step-wise supervision, although recently more interesting ways to use the trajectories, such as Hint-ReLIC [21], were proposed.

paragraphs.en: That is, a single (G)NN, capable of executing sorting, path-finding, convex hull finding, and all other CLRS algorithms. Since the input and output dimensionalities can vary wildly between the different algorithms, we would still propose using separate encoders and decoders for each algorithm—mapping into and out of the processor’s latent space—however, we deliberately keep these as linear functions to place the majority of the computational effort on P .
paragraphs.zh: 也就是说，用一个单一的（图）神经网络（(G)NN），就能够执行排序、寻路、凸包查找以及所有其他 CLRS 算法。 由于不同算法之间的输入和输出维度可能差异巨大，我们仍然建议为每种算法使用单独的编码器和解码器——分别映射到处理器 P 的潜在空间和从中映射出来——不过，我们刻意将这些保持为线性函数，以便把大部分计算工作都放在 P 上。

paragraphs.en: However, despite the base idea being simple in principle, this proves to be no trivial endeavour. Accordingly, our initial single-processor multi-task training runs on all of CLRS-30 resulted in NaNs.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，尽管其基本思想在原理上很简单，事实证明这绝非一件轻而易举的事。 此前大多数学习多种算法的尝试，例如 NEGA [7] 及其后续工作 NE++ [45]，都刻意聚焦于学习执行高度相关的算法，其学习信号很可能具有良好的相关性。 因此，我们在全部 CLRS-30 上进行的初始单处理器多任务训练运行出现了 NaN。

paragraphs.en: While it is evident from this plot that we still have a long way to go before we produce a fully “algorithmic” NAR processor library, this result has been seen as a significant “compression” milestone, similar to the Gato [47] paper. The release of our Triplet-GMPNN model sparked extremely interesting discussions on Twitter , Reddit and HackerNews , especially in light of its implications to constructing generally-intelligent systems. paragraphs.en: Needless to say, there is a lot of material this article does not cover—especially, the technical and implementation details of many of the papers discussed herein. If what you’ve read here has made you interested to know more, or even play with NAR models yourself, I recommend you check out the LoG’22 Tutorial on NAR ( https://algo-reasoning.github.io/ ), which I delivered alongside Andreea Deac and Andrew Dudzik . Over the course of just under three hours, we cover all of the theory needed to master the foundations of developing, deploying, and deepening neural algorithmic reasoners, along with plentiful code pointers and references. paragraphs.en: Petar Veličković is a Staff Research Scientist at Google DeepMind , Affiliated Lecturer at the University of Cambridge , and an Associate of Clare Hall, Cambridge . Petar holds a PhD in Computer Science from the University of Cambridge ( Trinity College ), obtained under the supervision of Pietro Liò . His research concerns geometric deep learning —devising neural network architectures that respect the invariances and symmetries in data (a topic he's co-written a proto-book about).
paragraphs.zh: Petar Veličković 是 Google DeepMind 的资深研究科学家、剑桥大学的附属讲师，以及剑桥大学克莱尔学堂（Clare Hall）的准会员（Associate）。 Petar 在 Pietro Liò 的指导下于剑桥大学（三一学院）获得计算机科学博士学位。 他的研究方向是几何深度学习——设计能够尊重数据中的不变性与对称性的神经网络架构（他曾与人合著过一本关于该主题的雏形书）。
